paper_title: Lifting for Constant-Depth Circuits and Applications to MCSP
classifications: Theory of computation → Problems, reductions and completeness
statement: One obvious question is whether one can show the NP-completeness of AC0d -MCSP for any constant depth d ≥ 3 by proving that depth 3 circuit complexity is NP-hard to approximate to within the factors needed by our lifting theorems? Note that while we have hardness of approximation result for DNFs [23, 3], the (almost tight) approximation gap there is not strong enough for our lifting theorems to apply. For depth-3 circuits, on the other hand, there are no known hardness of approximation results.
context: 6 Open Questions One obvious question is whether one can show the NP-completeness of AC0d -MCSP for any constant depth d ≥ 3 by proving that depth 3 circuit complexity is NP-hard to approximate to within the factors needed by our lifting theorems? Note that while we have hardness of approximation result for DNFs [23, 3], the (almost tight) approximation gap there is not strong enough for our lifting theorems to apply. For depth-3 circuits, on the other hand, there are no known hardness of approximation results. Another natural question is to tighten the gap (the approximation factor) of our lifting theorems. Finally, can one provide more evidence supporting the Weak Exponential Time Hypothesis for AC0d -MCSP?
